summary: This bill updates the Undetectable Firearms Act of 1988 by changing the definition of an "undetectable firearm" to include any firearm that does not contain detectable material in all parts other than major components, and clarifies that the prohibition applies to prototypes and does not apply to firearms under the control of the U.S. government or those manufactured under contract for the U.S. government.

scores.thoughts: This bill aims to modernize the Undetectable Firearms Act of 1988 by updating definitions for 'major component' and 'detectable material' to ensure firearms remain detectable by security screening devices. This is a clear effort to strengthen existing gun regulations by closing potential loopholes related to undetectable firearms.

The bill amends federal law regarding undetectable firearms, which are illegal. By modernizing the definitions and scope of what constitutes an undetectable firearm, it strengthens the legal framework for prosecuting offenses related to such weapons, thereby contributing to stricter enforcement of gun laws.
